# Tooling Dependencies

The project's runtime guideline is "no dependencies in runtime, Zig-only with as few build-time dependencies as possible." This file captures the few external tools that remain, and how they are integrated.

### Parser generated straight to Zig by the langlang fork

**Decision.** The `.circ` parser is generated by the maintainer's [langlang fork](https://github.com/jeffersonmourak/langlang) with `-output-language zig`: one self-contained `lib/parser/parser.zig` that holds the fork's PEG virtual machine (`go/zig/langlang_runtime.zig`, all 33 opcodes including left recursion, pasted as `pub const runtime`) followed by the grammar's bytecode as `comptime` tables and a `Rule` enum. circ vendors that file; `lib/syntax/translate.zig` walks `parser.runtime.Tree` into the AST. This is decision 1 of the libcirc plan.

**Rationale.** The runtime is complete and lives with the generator, so a grammar change is `edit .peg → zig build parser:gen → review goldens` and never needs parser work in circ, however many opcodes the grammar comes to use. Parity with the reference Go virtual machine was proven on the langlang side (`TestGenZigDifferential` over the circ grammar, `TestGenZigTablesMatchVendoredGo`, and `go/zig/scripts/diff-circ.sh` at 0 mismatches over every `.circ` fixture in this repository) before the cut-over.

**Alternatives.** A circ-local bytecode VM (tracks langlang's instruction set by hand and breaks on the next opcode). A hand-written recursive-descent parser (the grammar becomes prose). A Go `js/wasm` sidecar (2 MB of Go runtime and a second linear memory in the browser). Wrapping the old c-archive for wasm (impossible: Go refuses `c-archive` for wasm targets).

**History.** Until the cut-over the parser was `lib/parser/parser.go` plus a hand-written `shim/shim.go`, built at every `zig build` by `go build -buildmode=c-archive` into `parser.a`/`parser.h` and linked through `lib/syntax/CParser.zig`. That bridge cost ~2 MB of Go runtime per binary, a Go 1.21+ prerequisite for every contributor, no Windows cross-compile, and no route to `wasm32-freestanding` at all — which is what made a browser build of the compiler impossible.

### The fork's tag is the pin; the generated header is the skew signal

**Decision.** The generator is pinned by the fork's release tag: `go install github.com/jeffersonmourak/langlang/go/cmd/langlang@v0.0.13-zig.2` (the fork's module path is `github.com/jeffersonmourak/langlang/go`; the tag is `go/v0.0.13-zig.2`), a fork of upstream `go/v0.0.12` — the exact generator that produced the last Go parser byte for byte. What a reviewer compares against the fork is the vendored file's third header line, `Runtime: langlang_runtime.zig abi=1 sha256=…`, together with the pasted runtime's `abi_version` and `langlang_version` constants.

**Rationale.** A grammar change never needs runtime work, but a langlang bump that changes the bytecode ABI does, and that work lives in the fork; the header makes drift visible in the diff. The build-time version check the earlier entry promised was never implemented on `main` (`parser:gen` ran whatever `langlang` was on `PATH`); it exists now: `zig build parser:gen` runs `langlang -version` first and refuses anything that does not report `v0.0.13-zig.2` — upstream `go/v0.0.12` would otherwise fail on `-output-language zig` with `Output language \`zig\` not supported`. A tag bump changes that literal in `build.zig` together with the install line in `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and the header comment of `lib/grammar/proto-circ.peg`.

**Alternatives.** Tracking the fork's branch head (a moving target). Trusting whatever `langlang` is on `PATH` (the header's sha256 would still catch drift, but only after a wrong regeneration lands in a diff).

### Generated parser is vendored in the repo

**Decision.** The generated `lib/parser/parser.zig` is checked into the repository. langlang is only required when the grammar (`lib/grammar/proto-circ.peg`) changes and the parser needs regeneration. Contributors who don't touch the grammar do not need langlang installed.

**Rationale.** Most users of the repo — including most contributors and all downstream consumers of the CLI — never modify the grammar. Requiring them to install langlang just to build is friction without benefit. Vendoring the generated source means the standard build path needs only Zig (plus Node for the behavioural test harnesses).

**Alternatives.** Generating the parser at every build. Always-current and avoids the "did someone forget to regenerate?" failure mode, but every build pulls in langlang as a hard prerequisite. The vendored approach trades that for a discipline of regenerating-and-committing whenever the grammar changes — a smaller and more localised burden.

### The contract was pinned before the switch

**Decision.** Before the parser changed, its observable contract was frozen on circ's side (decision 2): the AST golden dump gained an `Errors (n)` section listing every recovered error mark, twelve `tests/fixtures/circuits/recovery_*.circ` fixtures pinned the label-recovery spans, messages and parser quirks, and four `tests/fixtures/expected-analyze/*.json` goldens pinned the exact `--analyze` JSON — all generated by the Go parser and hand-reviewed. circ's fixtures also feed the fork's corpus-mode differential (`diff-circ.sh`), which compares node ids and spans, not only goldens.

**Rationale.** Every `expected-*` golden stayed byte-identical through the cut-over because the oracle was fixed first; a regeneration that disagrees is a finding, not something to accept.

**Alternatives.** Corpus, mutation and fuzz machinery inside circ (dropped: it de-risked a circ-local VM that was never built).

### Go retired in one cut-over

**Decision.** One slice vendored `parser.zig` and deleted `lib/parser/{go.mod,parser.go,shim/}`, the untracked `parser.a`/`parser.h`, `lib/syntax/CParser.zig`, the dead `lib/syntax/nodes/declaration.zig`, the archive link helper, the `parser:archive` step and its `GOOS`/`GOARCH`/`CC` block; there is no dual-parser build option (decision 9).

**Rationale.** The differential proof lives on the langlang side and circ's goldens are the acceptance, so nothing is gained by keeping two parsers in lock-step. The PR workflow gained a `Remove Go from PATH` step that prunes every `PATH` entry holding an executable `go` and fails if `command -v go` still resolves, because `ubuntu-latest` ships Go and could not otherwise prove independence; the full suite then builds `circ-compile` Go-free.

**Alternatives.** A `-Dparser=go|zig` switch (two parsers to keep in lock-step for no consumer).
